Container.Name: Fling
Container.Overview: Self-hosted file transfer. Drag files, folders or whole trees into the browser, get a short link that is easy to read out loud, and the recipient downloads individual files, folders as a zip, or everything at once.[br][br]Files are encrypted at rest with a master key held in /config. Uploads are chunked and resume after a dropped connection or a server restart.[br][br]IMPORTANT: create the two host directories and give them to nobody:users before starting the container, or the first boot cannot write its master key:[br]mkdir -p /mnt/cache/appdata/fling /mnt/user/fling-data[br]chown -R 99:100 /mnt/cache/appdata/fling /mnt/user/fling-data[br][br]Then open the WebUI at /admin and set an admin password.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the web interface.

Config.Name: Config (SQLite + master key)
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite database and master.key. Keep this on a CACHE-BACKED path (/mnt/cache/...), NOT /mnt/user — SQLite over Unraid's fuse mount can hit file-locking problems. Back up master.key: without it every stored file is unrecoverable.

Config.Name: Data (encrypted file blobs)
Config.Description: The encrypted blobs. Plain sequential I/O, so this is happy on the array.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Base URL used in generated share links, e.g. https://fling.example.com. Leave empty to derive it from the incoming request. Set it when you run behind a reverse proxy.

Config.Name: Admin password
Config.Description: Optional. Sets the admin password on EVERY boot while present, overwriting any change made in the admin page. Leave empty and claim the password by visiting /admin instead.

Config.Name: Trust proxy headers
Config.Description: Set to true ONLY when a reverse proxy is the sole route to this container. When on, X-Forwarded-For is taken at face value — and that header is what the rate limiter keys on, so a client that can reach the port directly can rotate it and sidestep the admin-login and slug-lookup limits.

Config.Name: Timezone
Config.Description: Timezone used for logs and expiry timestamps.

Config.Name: Master key
Config.Description: Optional. 32-byte key as base64 or 64 hex chars — generate with: openssl rand -base64 32. Leave empty to have one generated into /config/master.key on first boot. Either way, BACK IT UP. Changing this after files exist makes them unreadable.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: Pino log level: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal.
